lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Now you two — Trophonius, Amphilochus — you're dead, and somehow you've been awarded temples, and you pass for prophets, and the fools upstairs have got it into their heads that you're gods.
lines.description: cheerfully incredulous, laying out the absurdity as simple fact

lines.speaker: Amphilochus
lines.text: And how is that our fault, if they're idiotic enough to think such things about a couple of corpses?
lines.description: defensive but dry, shrugging off responsibility

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: They wouldn't think it if you hadn't been putting on the same act while you were alive — playing the wonder-worker, pretending you knew the future, promising answers to anyone who asked.
lines.description: amused prosecution, ticking off charges without heat

lines.speaker: Trophonius
lines.text: Menippus, Amphilochus here can answer for himself. As for me — I am a hero, and I do give oracles, to anyone who comes down to consult me. You sound like a man who's never actually been to Lebadeia. Otherwise you wouldn't be so dismissive.
lines.description: pompous, wounded authority; selling the shrine hard

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Oh, is that so? You mean unless I trot off to Lebadeia, get myself rigged up in ridiculous linen robes, take a barley-cake in both hands, and squeeze through that miserable little hole into your cave — unless I do all that, I can't possibly tell that you're a corpse like the rest of us, the only difference being the stage business? [pause] But come — in the name of your prophetic art — what exactly is a 'hero'? I genuinely don't know.
lines.description: delighted mock-logic, vivid ritual details; then innocent question

lines.speaker: Trophonius
lines.text: A compound. Part man, part god.
lines.description: solemnly concise, pleased with the definition

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So — by your own account — neither a man nor a god, and somehow both at once. [pause] And the divine half of you — where's it gone off to just now?
lines.description: deadpan deduction, then soft pounce on the contradiction

lines.speaker: Trophonius
lines.text: It's giving oracles, Menippus. In Boeotia.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Trophonius, I have no idea what you're talking about. What I can see, perfectly clearly, is that the whole of you is dead.
